text:
devon: Hey team — quick payroll question. I was a contractor (1099-NEC) through 2025-04-18 while living in PA, then converted to a full-time Redwood employee starting 2025-04-21 after I moved to NY. My 1099 shows state withholding from PA (~$900) and my W-2 shows NY withholding for the rest of the year. Looks like I got taxed twice at the state level for income around the conversion date. Can someone advise next steps?

lina-payroll: Thanks for flagging this, Devon. Short answer: we need to confirm whether the PA withholding on the 1099 was employer-side backup withholding or a vendor payroll error. 1099s normally don't have state withholding unless vendor applied it. Do you have the 1099-NEC PDF and the W-2 handy?

devon: I attached the 1099-NEC and W-2 pdfs to my Workday record and pasted the paystub that shows the PA state line and the W-2 showing NY state wages.

mike-accounting: Quick note: if the company mistakenly withheld PA taxes while you were paid as a contractor, we can either (A) request a refund/adjustment from the PA vendor/payroll provider and issue a corrected 1099-NEC (1099-NEC correction), or (B) provide documentation so you can claim a credit on your NY return for taxes paid to PA. Which path depends on vendor timelines.

sam-peopleops: Adding context — since you changed residency mid-year, you'll likely file NY nonresident/part-year returns (NYS IT-203) and PA part-year (PA-40) if required. We should coordinate with tax counsel to avoid double taxation and decide whether to push for employer-side refund vs employee claiming credit.

lina-payroll: I've opened ticket PR-4412 to investigate with our contractor vendor and payroll ops. payroll-bot: PR-4412 created by lina-payroll. Status: investigating.

lina-payroll: Operational plan: 1) confirm nature of PA withholding recorded on the 1099 (was it 'state tax withheld' field set by vendor?), 2) if vendor withheld in error, request corrected 1099-NEC (box 4/16 adjustments) and refund, 3) if vendor cannot refund, compile a statement of employer-collected taxes so Devon can claim a credit on NY return, 4) if W-2 is impacted by retro adjustments, consider W-2c issuance.

devon: If you do issue a corrected 1099, will that change my 2025 tax filings? I'm worried about deadlines.

mike-accounting: If we get a corrected 1099-NEC (or vendor issues a refund), that will reduce your reported state withholding and likely avoid the need for a credit claim. If refund is slow, you can still file and claim a credit on IT-203. We'll provide a payroll statement showing the duplicate withholding and a timeline for the correction.

lina-payroll: Example of the internal update I'll request from the vendor (pseudo API):
```
PATCH /vendor/payruns/5567/worker/98765
{
  "adjustments": [
    {"type":"state_withholding_refund","state":"PA","amount":900}
  ],
  "request_correction_forms": ["1099-NEC"]
}
```

sam-peopleops: Tax counsel note — confirm residency dates and retain proof of move (lease/utility + travel stamp). If refund can't be obtained, employee may be eligible for a credit or amended return in PA depending on filing details.

devon: I uploaded lease + move confirmation email to the ticket. Anything else you need?

lina-payroll: That's perfect. Also confirm SSN and the date you provided it so we can trace vendor matching errors.

tax-bot: PR-4412 updated: vendor outreach sent. ETA vendor response: 7-10 business days.

mike-accounting: If vendor can't correct the 1099 this tax year, we'll prepare a formal employer statement that itemizes gross pay, taxes withheld by vendor, and dates of conversion. Devon can use it to claim a credit or to file an amended PA return. Also flagging potential W-2/W-2c coordination if we adjust employer-side records.

devon: Appreciate the plan. One last Q — will this generate any employer-side tax liabilities? I don't want this to affect my team.

lina-payroll: Usually employer-side refunds don't change your employment status. If the vendor refunds state withholding to the employer, we’ll issue a corrected 1099 to you. Any employer tax exposures are handled between Accounting and the vendor. We'll update PR-4412 with outcomes.

payroll-bot: PR-4412 status: vendor responded — correction requested. Next update expected: 2025-05-10.

devon: Great — thanks everyone :slightly_smiling_face: please keep me posted.

lina-payroll: Will do. Closing loop in the ticket once we have corrected forms or a documented refund path. :thumbsup:
